Apple drops after Trump threatens tariffs on iPhones from China
Edward Dufner , Bloomberg News
Customers look at new Apple iPhones on display including the iPhone XS, front, at an Apple store in New York on Friday, Sept. 21, 2018. , The Canadian Press Security Not Found See Full Stock Page »
Apple Inc. ( AAPL.O ) fell in extended trading after President Donald Trump told the Wall Street Journal that U.S. tariffs could be placed on iPhones imported from China.
Trump also told the newspaper that he expects to move ahead with increasing duties on goods from China to 25 per cent.
Apple fell 1.5 per cent to US$171.88 at 4:26 p.m. in New York following the Journal’s report on Trump’s remarks.
